business_problem: Timefold needed elastic, CPU-optimized infrastructure that could ingest large client scheduling datasets, solve complex combinatorial optimization problems in real time, and satisfy enterprise security and data-localization requirements without burdening a young team with infrastructure overhead.
solution_summary: Timefold runs its scheduling-optimization SaaS on a microservices architecture built around Google Kubernetes Engine so the platform can automatically absorb demand spikes and allocate compute where scheduling workloads are heaviest. The company combines GKE with flexible Compute Engine machine choices for CPU-bound optimization jobs, while Cloud Storage, Artifact Registry, Cloud Monitoring, Cloud Logging, and Identity and Access Management provide the storage, deployment, observability, and security controls needed for enterprise delivery. Client data is processed in real time to model skills, availability, labor rules, and routing constraints, then fed into optimization engines that recalculate schedules across entire workforces and fleets instead of assigning work incrementally. Google Cloud's regional footprint also lets Timefold stand up isolated environments in Europe, the United States, and dedicated customer clusters.

solution_components.name: Compute Engine

solution_components.name: Cloud Storage

solution_components.name: Artifact Registry

solution_components.name: Cloud Monitoring

solution_components.name: Cloud Logging

solution_components.name: Identity and Access Management (IAM)

solution_components.name: Gemini
solution_components.role: Supports internal development analysis and the Timefold Copilot natural-language scheduling experience.
